partnershipPlan: Two stroke survivors review the patient information on fast-track CT; a paramedic and a CT radiographer attend every monthly review.
socialListening: No social media listening; the regional stroke association's feedback from members about emergency care is read for themes.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I lay in the corridor for what felt like ages before anyone told me I was having a scan.
items.implication: Direct-to-CT and a clear word to the patient at the door.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: By the time the third person has been called, the patient has already been in CT for five minutes and nobody is there.
items.implication: Test a single group page on pre-alert.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: We would happily take them straight to the scanner if someone met us at the door.
items.implication: Stroke nurse meets pre-alerted ambulances at the door.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: If a stroke is on the table and a major trauma rolls in, somebody waits, and I need to know who decides.
items.implication: Agree a scanner priority rule and log conflicts.

summary: Four composite voices on waiting, paging, paramedic handover and scanner conflicts.
